title: TemplateLeak: A Template-Disjoint Evaluation Audit of CommonForms Form Field Detection

contributions.purpose: Provide a principled way to test whether template overlap between train/test splits inflates detection metrics in document understanding benchmarks.
contributions.mechanism: TemplateLeak audit framework combining MinHash/LSH clustering of form pages by field-layout similarity with document-level permutation testing.
contributions.evaluation: Applied to CommonForms (nearly 500,000 pages); partitions test set into Overlap-Test and Novel-Test slices and runs a 1000-permutation null test.
contributions.domain: form field detection / document understanding benchmark auditing
contributions.source_quote: We introduce TemplateLeak, a principled audit framework combining MinHash clustering with permutation testing to assess template-disjointness in document understanding benchmarks.

contributions.purpose: Determine whether CommonForms suffers from template leakage that would invalidate standard mAP evaluation.
contributions.mechanism: Comparing observed template overlap fraction against a permutation null distribution to assess statistical significance.
contributions.evaluation: Template leakage hypothesis refuted: observed overlap 26.8% at tau=0.80 falls below null mean 28.6% (z=-0.70, p=0.737); mAP gap of +12.9 between Overlap-Test and Novel-Test cannot be attributed to memorization.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that CommonForms is effectively template-disjoint at the field-layout level, refuting concerns about template leakage inflating detection metrics.

contributions.purpose: Establish robustness of the template-disjointness conclusion.
contributions.mechanism: Sweeping the Jaccard similarity threshold across four values and re-running the audit.
contributions.evaluation: Conclusion robust across four similarity thresholds (tau=0.50 to 0.95), with all z-scores negative.
contributions.source_quote: We show that the audit conclusion is robust across four similarity thresholds (tau = 0.50 to 0.95), with all z-scores negative.

self_declared_provenance.quote: The recently released CommonForms dataset (Barrow, 2025) provides the largest benchmark for this task, containing nearly 500,000 form pages with bounding box annotations.

Benchmarks such as VRDU (Wang et al., 2022) and DocLayNet (Pfitzmann et al., 2022) have highlighted that forms often share common layouts, and document-level splitting may not prevent template-level leakage.
To efficiently cluster pages by template similarity, we employ MinHash with Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) (Broder, 1997).

notes: NEGATIVE / REFUTATION RESULT: the paper's central finding refutes its own template-leakage hypothesis (observed overlap 26.8% is BELOW the null mean 28.6%, z=-0.70, p=0.737, not significant). Despite a +12.9 mAP gap between Overlap-Test and Novel-Test slices, the audit concludes CommonForms is template-disjoint and standard mAP is valid.
